title: radius: More dictionary updates
description:
More updates to the latest FreeRADIUS 3.2.4 dictionaries. These are
cases where Wireshark has some additions or tweaks to the FreeRADIUS
versions.

Note the switch from the FreeRADIUS pre 4.0 H3C dictionary to the 3.2.4
one. Identical other than including the Vendor name in the attribute,
as we do everywhere else. (It's a style change on FreeRADIUS's part
for 4.0.)

Update our README to note some of the changes.

Also delete the DHCP and VQP dictionaries, which are not for RADIUS
at all and which we don't use.

This does not include any updates to the 3gpp, 3gpp2, or wimax
dictionaries, which are large, along with one or two others that
would need TLVs unwrapped first. We also have still not done the
separation of the illegal attributes for usr and ascend into
separate files.

Add an .editorconfig file, since these use tabs

Ping #15458

I noticed a difference between CMake installation and Windows (NSIS) installation and the Windows installation doesn't include the .editorconfig file.
Is the bug that the NSIS installer should include the file (because of the tabs) or should CMake installation filter it out?

How is it getting installed? I don't see it in any of our CMake files. I'd vote for not installing it since plopping a hidden file somewhere on your system that changes your editor's behavior seems like a [POLA violation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principle_of_least_astonishment).

My CMake isn't that strong, but I would guess that having resources/protocols/radius in the INSTALL_DIRS list is just doing a *.* copy into the installation.
Maybe need to add
`PATTERN ".editorconfig" EXCLUDE`
to the
```
install(
	DIRECTORY
		${INSTALL_DIRS}
...
```

lines?

commits_data.title: radius: Move the illegal elements in ascend and usr to new files
commits_data.message:
radius: Move the illegal elements in ascend and usr to new files

Match FreeRADIUS, and move the illegal elements from the Ascend and
USR dictionaries to a new file. This means that a user has to only
uncomment one file instead of many entries.

The illegal dictionaries are moved to being after the conflicting
IETF ones, because the last attribute wins, so presumably if the
user uncomments them the user wants to override the IETF ones.

Remove a few duplicates from the USR dictionary, and match formatting.

Ping #15458. Ping #15551

commits_data.title: radius: More dictionary updates
commits_data.message:
radius: More dictionary updates

More updates to the latest FreeRADIUS 3.2.4 dictionaries. These are
cases where Wireshark has some additions or tweaks to the FreeRADIUS
versions.

Note the switch from the FreeRADIUS pre 4.0 H3C dictionary to the 3.2.4
one. Identical other than including the Vendor name in the attribute,
as we do everywhere else. (It's a style change on FreeRADIUS's part
for 4.0.)

Update our README to note some of the changes.

Also delete the DHCP and VQP dictionaries, which are not for RADIUS
at all and which we don't use.

This does not include any updates to the 3gpp, 3gpp2, or wimax
dictionaries, which are large, along with one or two others that
would need TLVs unwrapped first. We also have still not done the
separation of the illegal attributes for usr and ascend into
separate files.

Add an .editorconfig file, since these use tabs

Ping #15458
